Follow Hard After
FOL-oh hard AF-ter
verb phrase (Psalm 63:8)
From the Authorized Version rendering of the Hebrew dabaq, “to cleave, cling, pursue closely”; the soul's ardent pursuit of God in Psalm 63.

Biblical Definition

“My soul followeth hard after thee” is the cry of David in the wilderness of Judah, longing for God as in a dry and thirsty land where no water is. The Hebrew word rendered “followeth hard” is dabaq, the very word used of a man cleaving to his wife and of one clinging fast to another; it pictures not a casual seeking but a pressing, clinging pursuit that will not let go. The phrase names the holy ardour that ought to mark the believer's walk: a soul that thirsts for God, that follows close upon Him, that presses toward the mark, as the apostle says, for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. It is the spirit of Caleb, who followed the LORD fully and had another spirit with him, and the spirit of Jacob, who would not let the Angel go except He blessed him. Yet the same verse guards against a false notion of this pursuit, for David adds at once, “thy right hand upholdeth me.” The soul follows hard after God only because God upholds the soul; the cleaving is real and active, yet it rests upon a prior grace. The dictionary marks the phrase as the answer both to spiritual sloth, which seeks God faintly if at all, and to a proud self-effort that forgets the upholding hand; true pursuit of God is ardent and wholehearted, and wholly dependent on the grace that draws it.

Webster 1828 Definition

David's cry that his soul cleaves and presses close after God (Psalm 63:8); the holy ardour of wholehearted pursuit of the LORD, itself upheld by His sustaining grace.

FOLLOW HARD AFTER, verb phrase. [Hebrew dabaq, to cleave or cling closely.] To pursue God with clinging, pressing ardour.

David's soul followed hard after God in the wilderness, thirsting for Him as for water.

The same word describes a man cleaving to his wife and the saint clinging to the LORD.

It answers to the apostle's pressing toward the mark (Philippians 3:14) and to Caleb's following the LORD fully.

The pursuit is upheld by God's right hand, an active cleaving that rests upon prior grace.

Key Scripture

Ps 63:8 — "My soul followeth hard after thee: thy right hand upholdeth me."

Php 3:14 — "I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus."

Nu 14:24 — "But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it."

Ps 42:1 — "As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God."

Modern Corruption

The phrase is corrupted when ardent pursuit of God is collapsed either into a lazy “letting go and letting God” or into a striving that forgets the upholding hand of grace.

expand to see more

A strain of modern piety, reacting against works-righteousness, has made all active pursuit of God suspect, urging believers to cease striving and merely rest. But David did not rest passively; his soul followed hard after God, cleaving and pressing as a man cleaves to his bride. The dictionary names the quietist error: Scripture commands an ardent, wholehearted seeking of the Lord, and the gospel of grace does not abolish the pursuit but fuels it.

The opposite error is the proud self-effort that follows hard after God as though the cleaving were its own achievement. Against this David sets the second half of his verse: “thy right hand upholdeth me.” The soul cleaves because it is held; the pursuit is real and strenuous, and it rests wholly upon the prior and upholding grace of God. So Paul, who pressed toward the mark, could say in the same breath, “I laboured… yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me” (1 Corinthians 15:10). True pursuit is ardent and dependent at once.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew dabaq, to cleave, cling, or follow hard; the same word for marital union (Genesis 2:24) and for clinging to the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:20).

expand to see more

Dabaq, Hebrew, to cleave, cling, adhere, or pursue closely.

The same verb in Genesis 2:24 describes a man cleaving to his wife.

In Deuteronomy 10:20 the people are commanded to cleave (dabaq) unto the LORD.

The Greek dioko in Philippians 3:14, “I press,” carries the same note of strenuous pursuit.

The upholding “right hand” (Hebrew yamin) grounds the pursuit in sustaining grace.

Usage

"The pastor urged the young believers to follow hard after God, not to rest in a passive piety that seeks Him faintly."

"She marked that David's clinging was upheld by God's right hand, lest she trust her own pursuit."

"He preached Caleb's “another spirit” as the picture of a soul that follows the LORD fully."
